evidence: Hor. Epod. 2.4: faenore omnī solūtus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short prefers faenus to fēnus. To lend at interest, pecūniam faenorī dare (Traupman 333).

terms.gloss: interest; properly, the use of money lent
terms.comment: Reckoned by the month: centēsimae, one per cent a month (see rate).

phrases.latin: nec umquam sine ūsūrā reddit quod accēpit
phrases.english: (the earth) never returns what it has received without interest

phrases.latin: faenus ex triente Īdibus Quīntīlibus factum erat bessibus
phrases.english: on the Ides of July interest had gone up from a third to two thirds of a per cent a month

sources: Lewis & Short: faenus · Lewis & Short: usura
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. interest.
